deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics. It is a memorandum headed "Abgehende Posten in Göttingen" (departing mail coaches in Göttingen). The notebook is used upside down here, continuing the inverted 'Memor.' notes on the lower half of the previous page, which is dated around 1 Jan 1837.

Notation: weekdays are written with planetary symbols: ☉ Sunday, ☽ Monday, ♂ Tuesday, ☿ Wednesday, ♃ Thursday, ♀ Friday, ♄ Saturday. 'ab' is departure from Göttingen, 'an' is arrival in Göttingen, 'Morg.' morning, 'Ab.' evening, 'Nachm.' afternoon. Times are in hours, so 5½ʰ means 5:30.

Structure:
(A) Letter posts (riding posts):
- I. Hannover course, with three branches:
  - 1) side post of the Harz;
  - 2) over the Solling and Beverungen to the Lippe territory, Pyrmont, Rinteln and the Prussian provinces in Westphalia;
  - 3) letters by 'fahrende Post' (the coach post) to Hannover, Bremen, Osnabrück, Nienburg, Minden, Hameln, Hildesheim, Einbeck and Northeim. These leave Friday evening at 9½ and arrive Thursday morning at 3½.
- II. Frankfurt course. A sub-entry covers letters by coach post to Münden and Cassel.
- III. Eisenach via Witzenhausen.
- IV. Prussian course via Heiligenstadt.
- V. Duderstadt Landpost.
(B) 'Fahrende Posten' (coach posts):
- I. Hannover (noting 'also nicht Braunschw.', i.e. hence not to Braunschweig);
- 1) side course to Seesen and Braunschweig;
- 2) Seesen and the Braunschweig Weser district.

Each entry lists weekdays and clock times of departure and arrival. Nothing is derived or computed. It is a practical timetable Gauss copied for his own use.

results.what: Personal timetable of postal departures and arrivals at Göttingen (c. 1837), weekdays in planetary symbols

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a mail-coach timetable with no mathematical content. Gauss's habit of using planetary weekday symbols and keeping practical memoranda in his notebooks is well known.
transcription_corrections: 'Bevergern' should almost certainly read 'Beverungen'. That is the Weser town on the route over the Solling toward Pyrmont, and the manuscript appears to read 'Beverungen'.
'Lippeschen Pyrmont' should read 'Lippeschen, Pyrmont': three separate destinations, namely the Lippe territory, Pyrmont, and Rinteln.
In the last line, 'Braunsch. Wesel[?]' should read 'Braunschw. Weserdistrict' (the Braunschweig Weser district around Holzminden).

Several weekday symbol strings are uncertain in the machine transcription; ♂ versus ☽ and ♃ versus ♄ are easily confused in this hand. Examples are the first line 'ab ♂♃♀ Morg 5½' and 'Fahrende Posten I. ... ♃♄♀ Morg 3½'. These should be checked against the image.
In 'ab ♃ ʰ. 3½ʰ' (Münden/Cassel), the illegible word before 3½ is probably a time-of-day abbreviation such as 'Nachm.'.
The page is written upside down relative to the notebook. It continues the inverted 'Memor.' entries on the previous page (railway/postal notes).
